And you know, you just know it's going to be one of those conversations where he tells you something you disagree with and you're going to sit there and nod. Not because you think he's right, not because you don't have a better idea, but because you checked your bank account this morning. Rent is in 11 days and you literally cannot afford to have this conversation go badly. So, you nod, you
receipts.last_text_witness: again. You start thinking like someone with a floor. You start making decisions like someone who has options. Alex is still nodding in that meeting. Maybe you are too. The question isn't whether $3,000 a month is possible for you. The math says it is on almost any timeline with almost any income if the accumulation is consistent. The question is whether you're going to start building the floor or keep hoping the ceiling gets a little higher. Ceilings are controlled by other people. A floors are built by you.
